# Prose

The reading type. Wrap a document, CMS rich text, rendered Markdown or plain JSX, and its bare headings, lists, quotes, code and tables are typeset on Koala's tokens, with one size prop.

```tsx
<Prose>
  <h2>Constraints first</h2>
  <p>
    We started with constraints instead of components: four themes, one spacing
    scale and a fixed set of <strong>color roles</strong>. Read the{" "}
    <a href="/docs/foundations/colors">color foundations</a> for the full map.
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>Components never hard-code a value, they read tokens.</li>
    <li>A theme change is one file, not a hundred.</li>
  </ul>
  <blockquote>A component is only shared if it is easier to use than to rebuild.</blockquote>
  <p>Constraints feel limiting for about a week. After that they are the reason a new component takes an afternoon.</p>
</Prose>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add prose
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/prose/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { Prose } from "@/components/ui/prose"

export function Article({ html }: { html: string }) {
  return <Prose size="lg" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
}
```

## Sizes

The size picks the type and the rhythm together. `sm` is the 14px body of the product UI (a comment, a task description, what a RichTextEditor wrote); `md` is docs and release notes; `lg` is long-form reading at 17px, for an article at a ~42rem measure.

```tsx
<Prose size="sm">
  <h2>Release notes</h2>
  <p>Unified spacing across buttons, inputs and selects, so forms line up in dense dashboards.</p>
  <h3>Themes</h3>
  <p>The Moonlight theme gains contrast, and the branded focus ring follows it.</p>
</Prose>
```

```tsx
<Prose size="md">
  <h2>Release notes</h2>
  <p>Unified spacing across buttons, inputs and selects, so forms line up in dense dashboards.</p>
  <h3>Themes</h3>
  <p>The Moonlight theme gains contrast, and the branded focus ring follows it.</p>
</Prose>
```

```tsx
<Prose size="lg">
  <h2>Release notes</h2>
  <p>Unified spacing across buttons, inputs and selects, so forms line up in dense dashboards.</p>
  <h3>Themes</h3>
  <p>The Moonlight theme gains contrast, and the branded focus ring follows it.</p>
</Prose>
```

## Rich text from a CMS

A CMS, a Markdown renderer or a Tiptap export hands you a string of bare HTML. Set it on Prose and it is typeset as it is: no class to add to the content.

```tsx
const html = `<h2>Koala UI v11</h2><p>A major update focused on <strong>design system consistency</strong> …</p>…`

<Prose dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
```

## Elements

Ordered lists carry tabular markers, inline `code` keeps the global chip, a `pre` is a muted block that scrolls on its own, a table scrolls inside the column instead of the page, and a picture gets the corner radius and the image outline. Media take a wider step than copy, so they read as breaks.

```tsx
<Prose>
  <h3>Install</h3>
  <ol>
    <li>Add the package.</li>
    <li>Import <code>globals.css</code> once, at the root.</li>
  </ol>
  <pre><code>npx koalaui-cli add prose</code></pre>
  <figure>
    <img src="…" alt="A laptop on a desk, a code editor open" />
    <figcaption>The token map is the contract.</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <table>
    <thead><tr><th>Size</th><th>Body</th><th>Block step</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>sm</td><td>14 / 24</td><td>16px</td></tr>
      <tr><td>md</td><td>16 / 28</td><td>20px</td></tr>
      <tr><td>lg</td><td>17 / 28</td><td>24px</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
  <hr />
  <h4>Still stuck?</h4>
  <p>Every size shares these rules; only the scale and the spacing change.</p>
</Prose>
```

## Components inside

Prose styles bare elements. An anchor or image that carries a class is a component, so it keeps its own look: a `Link` or a `Button` dropped into the copy is never underlined or restyled.

```tsx
<Prose>
  <p>
    A bare <a href="#">anchor</a> wears the prose link; a{" "}
    <Link variant="prose" href="#">Link</Link> is the same treatment, as a component.
  </p>
  <p>
    <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">View template</Button>
  </p>
</Prose>
```

## As child

Pass `asChild` to put the styling on your own element, an `article` or a `section`, instead of a wrapping `div`.

```tsx title="article.tsx"
<Prose asChild size="lg">
  <article>
    <h2>Tokens over values</h2>
    <p>A card does not know it is twelve pixels of radius; it knows it uses the surface radius.</p>
  </article>
</Prose>
```

## FAQ

### Do I need @tailwindcss/typography?

No. Prose is one tv recipe on Koala's own tokens: the body is the `--body` reading ink, headings and bold lift to `--foreground`, list markers step down to `--muted-foreground`, links turn `--link` on hover. It re-themes across light, cream, dark and moonlight with no plugin.

### Why does the copy start flush with the top of the wrapper?

Rhythm is space between top-level blocks only, never before the first one or after the last. So Prose adds no gap to whatever it sits in, and you space it from its neighbours like any other block (`mt-8`).

### Which size should I use?

Match the surface. `sm` inside product UI, where the body around it is 14px (a comment thread, a panel, the read-only view of a RichTextEditor). `md` for documentation and release notes. `lg` for an article someone sits down to read, at a measure around 42rem.

### How do I style one element differently?

Give it a class, or pass a descendant utility on Prose itself, for example `className="[&_h2]:text-brand"`. It is merged last, so it wins over the recipe.

### Why is my Link or Button not underlined inside Prose?

By design. Prose only styles a bare `<a>` (no class); anything with a class is a component and keeps its own look. `Link variant="prose"` is the same treatment as the bare anchor, as a component, for when you write the copy in JSX.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add prose` writes `components/ui/prose/`. Import from `@/components/ui/prose`:

- Components and helpers: `Prose`, `proseVariants`
- Types: `ProseProps`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `tv`
- npm packages: `radix-ui`
